scope: Seven original AQA Chemistry 7405 AS 3.1.2 applied questions filling unverified Amount of Substance skills
notes: All numerical values are explicitly provided, no recall of gas or Avogadro constant expected. Original practice and provisional mark points, not official past-paper questions or mark schemes; manual review of unfamiliar valid workings and ECF is necessary.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Amount of Substance Applications
questions.question: Full and ionic equation for a precipitation reaction
questions.subtopic: Applied formulae, balanced equations and quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: Aqueous calcium chloride reacts with aqueous sodium carbonate to form insoluble calcium carbonate. Write a balanced full formula equation, including state symbols, then the net ionic equation. Identify the spectator ions. [5 marks]
markPoints: Correct full reactant and product formulae: CaCl₂, Na₂CO₃, CaCO₃ and NaCl.
Balanced full equation with two NaCl units: CaCl₂(aq) + Na₂CO₃(aq) → CaCO₃(s) + 2NaCl(aq).
The ionic equation contains Ca²⁺(aq) and CO₃²⁻(aq) on the reactant side.
Ionic product is CaCO₃(s), with both atoms and net charge balanced.
Correct spectator ions are Na⁺ and Cl⁻.
questions.modelAnswer: CaCl₂(aq)+Na₂CO₃(aq)→CaCO₃(s)+2NaCl(aq). Net ionic: Ca²⁺(aq)+CO₃²⁻(aq)→CaCO₃(s). The spectator ions are Na⁺ and Cl⁻. Charges sum to zero on each side.

questions.series: Original AQA-style Amount of Substance Applications
questions.question: Counting ions in an ionic compound
questions.subtopic: Applied formulae, balanced equations and quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: A sample contains 0.125 mol of MgCl₂. Assume every formula unit gives one Mg²⁺ ion and two Cl⁻ ions when dissolved. Given Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, calculate (a) the number of Mg²⁺ ions, (b) the number of Cl⁻ ions and (c) the total number of ions. Give all answers to 3 significant figures. [6 marks]
markPoints: One mol of MgCl₂ corresponds to one mol of Mg²⁺ and two mol of Cl⁻.
Amount of Mg²⁺ correctly identified as 0.125 mol.
Amount of chloride ions correctly calculated as 0.250 mol.
questions.modelAnswer: Each formula unit contains one Mg²⁺ and two Cl⁻. Thus n(Mg²⁺)=0.125 mol and n(Cl⁻)=0.250 mol. Numbers: 7.525×10²² → 7.53×10²² Mg²⁺; 1.505×10²³ → 1.51×10²³ Cl⁻ (3 sf); total 0.375×6.02×10²³ = 2.2575×10²³ → 2.26×10²³ ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Amount of Substance Applications
questions.question: Ideal gas equation with SI conversion and mass
questions.subtopic: Applied formulae, balanced equations and quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: A gaseous substance occupies 250 cm³ at pressure 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa and temperature 298 K. Its molar mass is 44.0 g mol⁻¹. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the amount in moles and the mass of the sample. Give both to 3 significant figures. [6 marks]
markPoints: Ideal gas equation pV=nRT stated or correctly rearranged n=pV/(RT).
Volume converted to SI units V=250×10⁻⁶ m³ = 2.50×10⁻⁴ m³.
Correct pressure and temperature substitutions: p=1.20×10⁵ Pa and T=298 K.
Mass found from m=nM using 44.0 g mol⁻¹.
Mass ≈ 0.533 g (3 sf), with correct units.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Amount of Substance Applications
questions.question: Titration stoichiometry of carbonate and acid
questions.subtopic: Applied formulae, balanced equations and quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: A 25.0 cm³ portion of sodium carbonate solution is neutralised by 23.40 cm³ of hydrochloric acid of concentration 0.100 mol dm⁻³. The equation is Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. Find the concentration of the Na₂CO₃ solution in mol dm⁻³ to 3 significant figures, showing each mole-ratio step. [6 marks]
markPoints: Correct conversion of acid volume to 0.02340 dm³.
Uses 2:1 HCl:Na₂CO₃ coefficient ratio.
Moles Na₂CO₃ in aliquot = 0.001170 mol.
Carbonate aliquot volume correctly converted to 0.0250 dm³.
Concentration = 0.001170/0.0250 = 0.0468 mol dm⁻³ (3 sf).
questions.modelAnswer: n(HCl)=cV=0.100×0.02340=0.002340 mol. The 2:1 stoichiometry means n(Na₂CO₃)=0.001170 mol. Sample V=25.0 cm³=0.0250 dm³. c(Na₂CO₃)=0.001170/0.0250=0.0468 mol dm⁻³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Amount of Substance Applications
questions.question: Atom economy using balanced coefficients
questions.subtopic: Applied formulae, balanced equations and quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: For the hypothetical stoichiometric equation 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O, sodium carbonate is the desired product. Use Mᵣ(NaHCO₃)=84.0 and Mᵣ(Na₂CO₃)=106.0 to calculate the percentage atom economy. Explain why the coefficient of NaHCO₃ matters. [5 marks]
markPoints: Correctly identifies Na₂CO₃ as the single desired product with relative formula mass 106.0.
Correctly uses TWO NaHCO₃ formula units as reactants, so reactant mass sum = 2×84.0=168.0.
Correct atom economy formula = mass of desired product / total reactant formula masses ×100.
Explains that the coefficient 2 is required for stoichiometric mass conservation; using 84.0 alone would be incorrect.
questions.modelAnswer: Atom economy=(Mᵣ of desired product)/(sum of Mᵣ values of reactants with balancing coefficients)×100. Here =106.0/(2×84.0)×100=63.095...%=63.1% (3 sf). The balanced coefficient means two formula units of NaHCO₃ are required to produce one Na₂CO₃.

questions.question: Empirical formula from masses and molecular Mr
questions.subtopic: Applied formulae, balanced equations and quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: A compound contains 0.720 g of carbon, 0.120 g of hydrogen and 0.960 g of oxygen. Calculate its empirical formula. Its relative molecular mass is 60.0; determine its molecular formula. Use Aᵣ(C)=12.0, Aᵣ(H)=1.0 and Aᵣ(O)=16.0. [6 marks]
markPoints: Moles hydrogen = 0.120/1.0 = 0.120.
Smallest whole-number mole ratio is C:H:O = 1:2:1.
Empirical formula CH₂O, whose relative formula mass is 30.0.
Molecular mass factor 60.0/30.0=2, giving molecular formula C₂H₄O₂.
questions.modelAnswer: n(C)=0.0600, n(H)=0.120, n(O)=0.0600 mol. Divide by 0.0600 to obtain 1:2:1, so empirical formula CH₂O. Empirical Mᵣ=12+2+16=30; molecular Mᵣ=60, a factor of two, giving C₂H₄O₂.

questions.question: Significant figures in a calculated concentration
questions.subtopic: Applied formulae, balanced equations and quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: A measured amount of solute is 0.00375 mol, made up to 50.0 cm³. Calculate the molar concentration in mol dm⁻³ and state how many significant figures your final answer should have based on the stated measurements. [4 marks]
markPoints: Converts 50.0 cm³ to 0.0500 dm³.
Uses c=n/V, with n=0.00375 mol.
Calculates 0.00375/0.0500=0.0750 mol dm⁻³.
Reports 0.0750 to THREE significant figures, matching the least precise stated measurements.
questions.modelAnswer: The volume is 0.0500 dm³. c=n/V=0.00375/0.0500=0.0750 mol dm⁻³. The significant digits are 7, 5 and the final 0, making three significant figures; both quoted data values have three significant figures.
